drug_class: Cholesterol-lowering combination medicine (cholesterol absorption inhibitor + statin)
purpose: This medicine is used to lower your bad cholesterol (LDL) and fats in your blood, while also raising your good cholesterol (HDL). It helps reduce your risk of heart attack and stroke. Doctors prescribe it when diet and exercise alone are not enough to control cholesterol.
how_it_works: This medicine works in two ways at the same time. The simvastatin part tells your liver to make less cholesterol on its own. The ezetimibe part blocks your intestines from absorbing as much cholesterol from the food you eat, so less cholesterol gets into your bloodstream.
common_side_effects: Muscle aches or weakness, headache, stomach pain or upset, nausea, and diarrhea are the most common side effects. Some people may feel unusually tired. Most side effects are mild and go away as your body adjusts.
warnings: Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially with fever or dark-colored urine — this can be a sign of a rare but serious muscle problem. Do not drink large amounts of grapefruit juice as it can increase side effects. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm your baby. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially certain antibiotics or antifungals, as they can interact dangerously with this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day in the evening. Common strengths include 10/10 mg, 10/20 mg, and 10/40 mg (ezetimibe/simvastatin). Your doctor will choose the right strength for you based on your cholesterol levels and other health factors. Try to take it at the same time each day.
